The source has been approached and has been asked if he is prepared to have his personal details conveyed to the Defence, and he has made -- he's adamant that he does not wish that to occur. As I understand it, the source also has no information as to the contact details or identity of the agent, and that's where matters stand. Mr. Emmerson has accurately reflected the situation. The Prosecution does not propose at this stage to provide any further details of the source at this stage. Prosecution is prepared to revisit the issue with the source in an endeavour to overcome this particular hurdle, but at this stage we're not prepared to disclose the contact details of the source.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The source -- the identity of that source itself is an information which falls upon the category of 68, does it not? MR. DI FAZIO: The information he provided. The source provided certain information to an investigator.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Not the identity itself is the Prosecution's position. MR. DI FAZIO: No. The source is known to the Prosecutor and the investigators. And the source, the person known as the source has been approached with a view to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In order not to -- MR. DI FAZIO: In order to provide his - that is, the source's - personal details to the Defence so that the Defence may make whatever inquiries it sees fit. The source has refused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: My question is whether the Prosecution does not need a protective measures permitted by the Chamber in order not to disclose the identity of that source. MR. DI FAZIO: It --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm just asking. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, yes. That may be. That may be a way of resolving this particular issue, but before we were to consent to that or agree to that I think it appropriate that we approach the source once more and see if the matter can be resolved in that fashion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I might make an observation. I believe the question you asked is, the question that needs to be addressed is not the identity of the source, him or herself, Rule 68 material, and I would observe that it is. And therefore there would be an affirmative duty --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yeah, that's the point of my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's what I thought it was, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So I would recommend the Prosecution to contact the source again, and in case it does not get the consent of the source come to the Court, come to the Chamber asking for the sort of protective measures. MR. DI FAZIO: With respect, that seems a sensible way of approaching the matter, and we're going to try and endeavour to resolve the issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We don't have much time. I guess that would resolve the issue of Witness 30.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would Your Honour say again, please, a response to that by the 25th?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would it fit -- how been end of month? MR. DI FAZIO: Well, there's every reason why we should not -- there's every reason to try and do that. Of course, it's not quite that easy because it's a live person who has to be contacted and arrangements made. Can I say that the Prosecution will do its utmost to address the issue and come to a final position and convey that to the Defence by the 25th? I just raise for the -- for the Defence and for the purposes of the Court that there may, there may be some difficulties in getting in touch with the -- with the source. That's the only difficulty that I envisage. Barring that impediment, I see no reason why the 25th should not be -- should not be a date by which we get the information to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you for that submission. I would put a deadline of 25th October, and if there's a -- a good cause on the part of the Prosecution the extension will be granted. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, as far as agreed facts are concerned, I'm not sure how much time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can I interrupt you there. I wonder -- give me a minute. I wonder the Defence for Mr. Brahimaj responded to the suggestion of the Prosecution for the agreed facts at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is there anything which was agreed upon among the suggested facts?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: There was a very limited number of matters on which we were able to offer agreement, largely for the same reasons that Mr. Emmerson outlined in respect of his client, that the proposed agreed facts were essentially amounted to admission to all of the allegations in the indictment. We did provide what we hoped would be a helpful series of questions to the Prosecution seeking a little elucidation of some of the items that -- on which they were seeking agreement so that we could see whether we could get a little bit closer to each other, but we've had no response to that. We did also indicate to the Prosecution that there were certain -- certain modifications that we would make to the propositions that they had propounded, and again we've had -- I'll be corrected if I'm wrong, I don't think we've had any response to that. So we've sought as much as possible to provide a constructive response, recognising that this is important to the Trial Chamber and to all the parties to get as close as possible to some kind of factual basis on which we share agreement, but that was provided some two months ago to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harvey. Can I suggest at this moment to the Prosecution to -- not to be too ambitious in getting the agreements from the Defence but be practical and modify or produce new sets of questions which might be practically easily agreeable by the Defence by the end of this month, and let's see what will come out later on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, certainly we'll comply with your suggestion. And also we've discussed with our learned friends during the break period the possibility of agreed facts coming particularly in the area of the forensics evidence but in other areas also. The Prosecution, and I believe the Defence counsel agree, that the Defence can suggest agreed facts, just as the Prosecution can suggest agreed upon facts, and that we would keep a very open spirit, both sides, in trying to narrow the issues before the Trial Chamber with what is not contested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think there's much, but how about adjudicated facts?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There is a possibility that we may actually be able to do some of that too. I believe based upon the conversations that we had during the break that we'll have a full inquiry by both sides to both of those areas. I don't know whether or not you intend on moving on to another area, and since the issue of agreed facts was mentioned I wanted to go back, if we could, just for a brief moment to the issue of disclosure, just as a general proposition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Because during the break I had an opportunity of a conversation with the Prosecution concerning their obligations under Rule 66 and Rule 68 and was informed, and I want to make sure I say this properly, not improperly, that they have fully met their obligations in disclosing those -- those areas of information to us at this juncture. So it is my understanding based upon that assertion that there is no outstanding information remaining except for new information that there may be available as a result of investigations. I'm going very slowly because I don't want to misspeak myself here. I am concerned about making sure that during the middle of trial or sometime during the trial we are not met with some witness statement which would fall under Rule 66 or Rule 68 which has been in the possession of the Office of the Prosecutor or some of their immediate agents for some period of time. And having been involved in a previous proceeding where that issue did arise, I wish to alert the Prosecution about my concern and was quite frankly pleased with the response that I should not have any concerns whatsoever because they have fully met their obligations. But if I've misspoken in any way about what the representation is, I believe Ms. Sellers is probably in a better position to say that I have or hopefully what she'll say is what Mr. Guy-Smith said is absolutely correct and then we won't have to go any further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure. Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might address you and Mr. Guy-Smith. I believe what I did say is very much in line with your representation to the Trial Chamber that we have fulfilled and are fulfilling our obligations under Rule 68, under Rule 66(A) and Rule 66(B). Nevertheless, it is possible, it is possible that while our continuing obligations are being fulfilled that there might be witnesses who prior to this time we didn't consider their statements as witness statements or relevant to this case, and so to have a blanket proposition that anything up until today has been disclosed, I think might be slightly misleading and I don't want to do that to the Trial Chamber. Also, I think that we are quite aware that we've already said that there are materials that we will be disclosing within the next couple of weeks. Those materials of course have come in before. And, Your Honour, there are certain instances where we do have to look at the very -- the utmost serious nature of witness protection with some material that we have that can be disclosed. So I think the spirit of what my learned friend is saying is certainly being complied with.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I thought it might be an appropriate point shortly after the question that the Chamber had asked with regard to the definition of Rule 68 material and perhaps the Prosecution would be encouraged to be more -- a bit more expansive in the manner in which they choose to define what Rule 68 is because I think we could potentially have a problem, had it not been from the Chamber's guidance, at that particular moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I see your point, and the point will be taken care of the Chamber. Let's leave the matter there. I'd like to ask question whether Prosecution is minded to file a motion for 92 bis or 92 ter witness statements and expert witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the simple answer is yes, we are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: When. The question should be when.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Then, Your Honour, in terms of the 92 bis statements, as we're in the process of finalising our witness list for the filing of the 65 ter, we would hope to soon after the finalising of that list, and in particular for witnesses that we believe will be called earlier on in the trial to file the 92 bis statements. In terms of the 94 ter statements, 94 bis statements, we'll do that within the procedural guidelines. What we would like to be able to do is to file and to have an open discussion with the Defence counsel. For those they don't oppose, let's move forward with that. I think that will also allow us to present the evidence in a fashion that's much more efficient and possibly much more rapid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: When do you practically envision such a motion will be filed?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: 92 bis and 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Well, the 92 bis of course would depend on the Defence pre-trial brief. The evidence that we would be presenting we would identify who we believe is to be 92 bis, if there is agreement reached on that type evidence, and I imagine that would be some of the issues that they would raise in their pre-trial brief, we'd be able to soon after then to commence our filing. For those witnesses that we think are 94 bis expert witnesses, I think that we have a clearer idea, and we're just awaiting some identification of one other expert and then some final reports that we would want to attach with expert -- our experts' reports or filings. In terms of the 94 quater, Your Honour, we would be going forward as soon as possible. Our intention is to put this before the Trial Chamber rapidly and to have decisions on the use of the evidence in that manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. And that will help the Chamber to assess the overall length of the trial in the future. And my intention is to have a next Status Conference just before or just after the winter recess, after having received the 92 bis and 92 ter motion and expert motion. And I will hear any urgent matters to raise at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think all parties have put trial date on their agendas as an issue to at least be raised at this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think I have anything to add to what is known at the moment. Next -- early next year will be all I can say, but we will address the issue as soon as possible. And I'd like to ask Mr. Balaj and Mr. Brahimaj if there's anything to say to the Chamber in relation to your custody or anything else. Mr. Balaj. THE ACCUSED BALAJ: [Interpretation] Your Honour, everything is in order. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Balaj. Mr. Brahimaj. THE ACCUSED BRAHIMAJ: [Interpretation] I don't have anything to add, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Brahimaj. I noticed Mr. Dutertre stood up for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, but I would not have taken the floor if you had not invited me to do so. I just wanted to inform the Chamber that currently at the Radonjic Lake and along the canal work is taking place and that the location is going to be altered, to be transformed. I just wanted the Chamber to be informed about the fact, and I wanted to put this on record. I don't have any further information about this specific matter. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, I think that concludes the Status Conference for today. For wrapping up, there are three assistants of Defence counsel to whom access will be allowed can be changed if there's agreement between the parties. That's my understanding.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. The hearing is now adjourned.
